title: Purification of DPP8/9 from Sf9 Cells for Structural and Biochemical Studies

Transfection efficiency is much higher with these plates cells. Adherence can be checked by examining plate(s) under a light microscope--cells should stay put when the plate is moved. The virus production protocol depends on the type of cells you use and the transfection reagent. This one works well, but there are other quicker protocols, too. All insect cell culture and virus manipulation should be done in a cell culture hood using proper sterile technique. Sterile spin steps can be done outside of the hood in tightly shut autoclaved containers. Insect cells are prone to fungi infection because they are grown at 27 degrees, which is evident from a strong smell and discoloration/particulates in the medium. Contaminated cells should be removed and bleached promptly.

Prepare and pre-chill the following buffers: Lysis buffer (100 mL, 25 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0, 150 mM NaCl, 1 mM tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine abbreviated as TCEP, 5 mM imidazole) Wash buffer (500 mL, 25 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0, 150 mM NaCl, 1 mM TCEP, 25 mM imidazole) Elution buffer (20 mL, 25 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0, 150 mM NaCl, 1 mM TCEP, 500 mM imidazole) Size exclusion buffer (500 mL, 25 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, 1 mM TCEP) 5 mM BME can be used as a reducing agent in lysis buffers and 2 mM DTT can be used in size exclusion buffers; however, avoid DTT for Ni-NTA steps. 1 mM TCEP can be used throughout. Reducing agent should be added fresh to all buffers. Imidazole should be pH adjusted to 8.0 before addition to any buffer. Avoid protease inhibitors, as DPP9 is a protease.

steps.title: Obtain Plasmids
steps.instruction: Obtain pFastBac HTB plasmids encoding the DPP of interest (DPP9 short or long isoform, WT or catalytically-inactive) from Addgene. For DPP8, use the cDNA from Addgene or the insect expression construct from Drs. Breyan Ross and Robert Huber.

steps.title: Transform DH10Bac Cells
steps.instruction: Transform ~100 ng of plasmid into ~50 uL of DH10Bac cells.

substeps.instruction: Follow standard transformation protocol, but incubate for 4 hours shaking at 37°C before plating (instead of 1 hour) to allow recombination and resistance protein production.
Perform serial dilutions (e.g., 10, 50, 100 ng of plasmid) across three separate batches of cells to optimize blue/white selection.

steps.title: Prepare Bacmid LB Agar Plates
steps.instruction: Prepare or purchase bacmid LB agar resistance plates containing 50 µg/ml kanamycin, 7 µg/ml gentamicin, 10 µg/ml tetracycline, 100 µg/ml Bluo-gal, and 40 µg/ml IPTG.

substeps.instruction: Cover plates in foil to protect doxycycline.
Store at 4°C (plates last less than 1 month).

steps.title: Plate and Incubate Cells
steps.instruction: Plate all cells from an individual transformation onto the prepared bacmid plates.

substeps.instruction: Wrap plates in foil.
Incubate at 37°C for 2 days.

steps.title: Select and Grow Colonies
steps.instruction: Pick at least 2 completely white colonies per construct and 1 negative control blue construct.

substeps.instruction: Grow colonies overnight in 5 mL of LB containing 50 µg/mL kanamycin, 7 µg/mL gentamicin, and 10 µg/mL tetracycline.

steps.title: Miniprep and Validate Bacmid
steps.instruction: Perform a bacmid miniprep to obtain purified bacmid (expected concentration 1-30 ug/uL).

substeps.instruction: Validate the insert via PCR using Q5 polymerase in 5-10 uL reactions.
Use M13 forward (5′-GTTTTCCCAGTCACGAC-3′) and reverse (5′-CAGGAAACAGCTATGAC-3′) primers.
Confirm the PCR product size is ~6000 bp (~2430 bp HT vector + ~2600 bp DPP8/9) compared to the negative control.

steps.title: Store Verified Bacmid
steps.instruction: Dilute verified bacmid(s) to 1000 ng/uL in endotoxin-free/sterile TE buffer.

substeps.instruction: Store at 4°C for short-term or -20°C for long-term storage.
Avoid freeze-thaw cycles.

steps.title: Prepare Transfection Complexes
steps.instruction: Prepare the bacmid and CellFectin II complexes using Grace's insect cell medium (warmed to room temperature).

substeps.instruction: Add 100 uL Grace's media to two autoclaved microcentrifuge tubes per construct.
Add 6 uL CellFectin II to one tube.
Add 1000 ng of bacmid to the other tube.
Transfer the bacmid-containing medium to the CellFectin II tube, pipette gently, and incubate for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Plate Sf9 Cells
steps.instruction: Plate 1.5 million cells from a suspension culture in a 6-well dish (1 well per construct plus 1 negative control).

substeps.instruction: Use room-temperature complete SFX to bring total volume to 1-2 mL per well.
Incubate the plate for at least 1 hour.

steps.title: Transfect Sf9 Cells
steps.instruction: Exchange the medium and introduce the transfection complexes to the Sf9 cells.

substeps.instruction: Wash cells once with 2 mL Grace's medium, remove, and add 1 mL Grace's medium to keep cells hydrated.
Add 800 uL Grace's medium to the transfection complex tubes (total volume >1 mL), mix gently, and transfer to the Sf9 wells.
Return plates to the 27°C incubator for 4-5 hours.

steps.title: Incubate and Grow Transfected Cells
steps.instruction: Replace the transfection medium with complete Sf9 medium.

substeps.instruction: Remove medium from each well and add 2 mL pre-warmed complete Sf9 medium.
Incubate for 3 days (can be extended to 5 days for sub-optimal efficiency).

steps.title: Generate P1 Virus
steps.instruction: Harvest the P1 virus from the cell culture supernatant.

substeps.instruction: Transfer supernatant to labeled microcentrifuge tubes.
Spin at 2000g (2000 rpm), 4°C, for 10 minutes to pellet cell debris.
Transfer the supernatant to fresh autoclaved tubes.

steps.title: Amplify P2 Virus
steps.instruction: Amplify the virus to P2 stage.

substeps.instruction: Remove medium from the original plate and add 1 mL fresh complete medium to each well.
Add 700 uL - 1 mL of P1 virus-containing medium to each well.
Incubate for 3 days.
Harvest P2 virus using the same centrifugation method as P1.

steps.title: Amplify P3 Virus
steps.instruction: Amplify the virus to P3 stage using a 15-cm plate.

substeps.instruction: Attach 15 million cells to a 15-cm plate and incubate for at least 1 hour at 27°C.
Add 1 mL of P2 virus and incubate for 3 days.
Harvest P3 virus into Falcon tubes (expected ~15 mL volume).

steps.title: Generate Baculovirus-Containing Cells (BIICs)
steps.instruction: Infect a larger suspension culture to produce BIICs.

substeps.instruction: Add 5 mL of P3 virus to a 200-mL suspension culture (at 2 million cells/mL).
Incubate for 2 days.
Harvest cells by centrifuging at 1000 x g, 4°C, for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Freeze and Store BIICs
steps.instruction: Prepare freezing medium (Complete SFX medium with 10% DMSO and 10% FBS) and store cells.

substeps.instruction: Remove medium from bottles and resuspend BIICs in freezing medium.
Aliquot into sterile microcentrifuge tubes (1 mL each).
Store at -80°C.

steps.title: Scale Up Protein Expression
steps.instruction: Express the protein in a 1 L suspension culture of Sf9 cells.

substeps.instruction: Grow suspension Sf9 cells to 1 L at 2 million cells/mL.
Thaw an aliquot of frozen BIICs and add to the insect cell flask.
Incubate for 2 days.

steps.title: Harvest and Prepare Cell Pellets
steps.instruction: Harvest the cells and prepare them for lysis.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge cells at 2500 rpm, 4°C, for 20 minutes.
Resuspend cell pellet in ice-cold PBS and transfer to 50 mL Falcon tubes.
Centrifuge at 2000 rpm, 4°C, for 20 minutes to remove medium components.
Gently remove PBS and either flash-freeze in liquid nitrogen for -80°C storage or proceed to purification.

steps.title: Cell Lysis and Clarification
steps.instruction: Lyse the cells and clarify the lysate via ultracentrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Thaw pellet and resuspend in 40 mL lysis buffer (per L of cells).
Transfer to a glass beaker in an ice-water bath and sonicate with a probe sonicator (3 s on, 5 s off, 3.5 min total on, 45% power, Branson Sonicator).
Centrifuge at 40,000 RPM, 4°C, for 1.5 hours (e.g., Beckman 45 Ti fixed-angle rotor).

steps.title: Ni-NTA Batch Binding
steps.instruction: Bind the protein to Ni-NTA resin.

substeps.instruction: Pre-equilibrate Ni-NTA resin (1 mL bed volume per 2L expression) with cold lysis buffer.
Carefully transfer the supernatant from the ultracentrifuge tubes to 50-mL Falcon tubes, avoiding the lipid layer and the cell pellet.
Add Ni-NTA beads to the tubes.
Fill tubes with cold lysis buffer to avoid bubbles and nutate/rock in the cold room for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Wash and Elute Protein
steps.instruction: Wash the resin and elute the target protein.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge resin at 800 x g, 4°C, for 5 minutes; remove supernatant.
Perform a batch wash by adding 20 CV wash buffer and centrifuging again (800 x g, 4°C, 5 min).
Remove supernatant, add 5 CV wash buffer, and transfer resin to a gravity column (e.g., Bio-Rad 7321010 or 7311550).
Wash the resin on-column with 25 CV ice-cold wash buffer.
Allow the bed to drain (do not let it dry), then incubate the resin with 3 CV ice-cold elution buffer in the cold room for 30 minutes, mixing gently.

steps.title: Concentrate and Polish Protein
steps.instruction: Concentrate the eluate and perform final purification.

substeps.instruction: Elute protein into an Amicon Ultra 100 kDa cutoff spin concentrator; use ~1 CV buffer to rinse the column.
Spin concentrate to ~0.5 mL at 4000 rpm, 4°C, and transfer to a microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 10000 rpm, 4°C, for 10 minutes to pellet aggregated protein.
Separate protein using a Superdex 200 increase 10/300 GL size exclusion column (Cytiva) with size exclusion buffer.

steps.title: Final Collection and Validation
steps.instruction: Collect and store the purified protein.

substeps.instruction: Collect peak fractions, concentrate, aliquot, and freeze as necessary (avoid freeze/thaw cycles).
Validate protein activity using a GP-AMC assay.
